            CE STEPHENS PROPERTIES, LLC’S REPLY TO EXCEPTIONS
                     TO THE PROPOSAL FOR DECISION

       CE Stephens Properties, LLC (CE Stephens) hereby files its Reply to Exceptions, and in

support thereof shows as follows:


I.     INTRODUCTION AND SUMMARY

       CE Stephens urges the Public Utility Commission of Texas (Commission) to affirm the

Administrative Law Judges’ (ALJs) Proposal for Decision (PFD) to deny Oncor/LCRA’s joint-

application in Docket No. 59475, and in the alternative, approve Route 894. The parties that

submitted exceptions (Excepting Parties) neither brought forth new arguments nor pointed to

record evidence not already dispensed with by the ALJs to persuade the Commission to reject the

ALJs’ finding that Alternative Route 894 is the route that best meets the Commission’s routing

criteria. A preponderance of the evidence fully supports the ALJs’ PFD.




SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349                   2          CE Stephens Properties, LLC’s Reply
PUC Docket No. 59475                                                 to Exceptions to the PFD
 II.       STANDARD OF REVIEW

          The Commission’s procedural rules outline the applicable standard of review that the

Commission must apply in this proceeding:

          Under 16 Texas Administrative Code (TAC) § 22.262(a):

          The commission may change a finding of fact or conclusion of law made by the

          administrative law judge … only if the commission … determines that the

          administrative law judge [either] . . . did not properly apply or interpret applicable

          law, commission rules or policies, or prior administrative decisions; or … issued a

          finding of fact that is not supported by a preponderance of the evidence … or

          determines that … a prior administrative decision on which the administrative law

          judge relied is incorrect or should be changed. 1

Applying the standard contemplated under § 22.262(a), above, the Commission may modify the

PFD, only if the Excepting Parties establish that the ALJs inadvertently supported a finding of fact

or erroneously applied the factors contemplated under PURA § 37.056 and 16 TAC § 25.101. The

Excepting Parties’ Exceptions to the PFD have failed to demonstrate such a showing.

          Specifically, the Excepting Parties identify individual metrics or localized impacts on

which Routes 487, 296, 572, or CCG may outperform Route 894. But not one of the Excepting

Parties demonstrated that the ALJs failed to consider the governing factors or that the balancing

reflected in the PFD is legally erroneous. For this reason, if the Commission approves a route, CE

Stephens respectfully urges the Commission to adopt the ALJs’ recommendation to approve Route

894.



1
      16 TAC § 22.262(a).

SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349                        3           CE Stephens Properties, LLC’s Reply
PUC Docket No. 59475                                                       to Exceptions to the PFD
        The routing factors set forth in PURA and the Commission’s Substantive Rule do not

require the ALJs to select the route that performs best on any one factor or metric. Rather, as the

PFD correctly recognizes, no statutory factor is absolute; the ALJs accordingly considered critical

factors such as cost, habitable structures, compatible-right-of-way paralleling, parks, river

crossings, environmental considerations, and cultural resources. Ultimately, the record evidence

demonstrated, and the ALJs agreed, that Route 894 performed as the best overall compromise

amongst these competing factors and interests.

       Crucially, the Excepting Parties seek nothing more than a different weighting of the same

evidence, rather than identifying omitted evidence or legal error. For these reasons and the reasons

discussed below, CE Stephens respectfully urges the Commission to adopt the ALJs’ PFD.


III.   REPLY TO EXCEPTIONS

       A preponderance of the evidence drives a finding that Route 894 best meets the

Commission’s routing factors. Neither Staff nor any intervenor has demonstrated the ALJs failed

consider evidence that would allow for a conclusion other than Route 894 best meets the

Commission’s routing factors. Moreover, neither Staff nor any intervenor has presented evidence

demonstrating the ALJs committed legal error.

       The record evidence demonstrates that Route 894 performs well in historically important

routing factors, such as habitable structures, cost, length, paralleling, and environmental integrity,

but more importantly, the record evidence demonstrates that, as a whole, Route 894 best overall

balances the routing criteria prescribed by 16 TAC §25.101. CE Stephens acknowledges that some

other route may perform better on a particular routing factor; nevertheless, the Commission is

tasked with selecting the route that best overall meets the Commission’s routing criteria while also

satisfying the Commission’s policy goal of Prudent Avoidance.

SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349                      4           CE Stephens Properties, LLC’s Reply
PUC Docket No. 59475                                                     to Exceptions to the PFD
         For instance, the Staff (Staff) of the Public Utility Commission of Texas (Commission)

recommended route, Route 487, has better paralleling that Route 894, costs 0.77% less, and is

0.75% shorter; crucially however, these are immaterial advantages and come at a cost that is not

justified. 2 Route 487 impacts 11 more (12.9%) habitable structures, crosses nearly 9 miles (21%)

more of riparian area, and comes within a 100 feet of Colorado Bend State Park. 3

        Route 296, advocated for by intervenors such as the G9 and G13 Landowners and Save the

Lampasas, may have slightly better paralleling 4 and crosses a marginally shorter length (5,539 feet

or 2.67%) 5 of riparian areas than Route 894. 6 But similar to Route 487, the slight advantages

Route 296 has over Route 894 in two routing factors are substantially outweighed by the fact that

Route 296 affects 21 more habitable structures, a staggering 24.7% increase over Route 894, Route

296 costs about $3.64 million more than Route 894, and is 3,250 feet longer than Route 894. 7

        Route 572, advocated for by parties such as Save the Lampasas and the Link N3 Opposition

Landowners, impacts 13,694 fewer feet of riparian areas, but crucially, the advantages stop there. 8

Route 572 impacts 22 more habitable structures, 25.8% more than Route 894, is 2.5 miles longer,

 costs $8.3 million more, 9 parallels 18,022 fewer feet of compatible ROW, and notably crosses

51,819 more feet (39.4%) of high archeological/historical site potential than Route 894. 10

          Route CCG, advocated for by parties such as Cherokee Creek Partners, does have better

paralleling than Route 894 and marginally fewer feet of the line crossing riparian areas. However,

similar to Routes 296, Route CCG impacts 20 more habitable structures than Route 894; is about

9 miles longer than Route 894; is approximately $73.7 million more expensive than Route 894;

and notably crosses 44,602 more feet (33.9%) of high archeological/historical site potential than

Route 894. 11

          At bottom, the Excepting Parties’ exceptions to the PFD provide no new arguments or

evidence that changes the fact that, overall, Route 894 best meets the Commission’s routing

criteria.


IV.       CONCLUSION

          At bottom, the Excepting Parties’ exceptions to the ALJs’ PFD ask the Commission to

reweigh evidence the ALJs expressly considered rather than identifying an error in the ALJs

balancing of the statutory factors, evidence the ALJs failed to consider, or legal error. And while

Route 894 quantitatively and qualitatively best satisfies the Commission’s routing criteria, CE

Stephens notes that it does not oppose Routes 392, 410, or 894 Western Mod.
